clue.text: Show some reason for military training?

parts.note: a show or display can be called a parade
a ground is a reason or basis, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A question about what justification there is for drilling soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place: the square where troops are drilled is the place for military training.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill square is the open space where soldiers practise marching and formation exercises.

clue.text: Old pedlar a Rugby forward ?

definitions.meaning: a travelling seller who carried his goods in a bundle on his back
the forwards in rugby are collectively called the pack, so one of them is a man of the pack

explanation.definitionFit: A hawker once carried a bundle of wares; a scrummaging player belongs to the eight forwards known as the pack.

clue.text: Upright type of citizen

definitions.meaning: the ordinary vertical typeface, as opposed to italic
a citizen of the ancient city on the Tiber

explanation.definitionFit: Non-italic printing is called roman type, and a native of Rome bears the same name.

clue.text: Suitable advice 'for Thomas, certainly

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it tells the sceptical apostle to question less; as one word it is an adverb of assurance.

clue.text: Profit is up for one horse-breaker

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the numeral breaks into the horse word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.walkthrough: 'horse-breaker' reads as a trainer of horses, but 'breaker' puts I inside NAG to give NIAG, which 'is up' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit and gain are synonyms for what is earned over cost.

clue.text: In an unusual manner, to beautify, perhaps

indicators.note: in an unusual manner suggests the letters are arranged out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Advice on beautifying something by doing it in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges MANNER and TO; 'perhaps' marks beautify as one example of what the verb can mean.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate or adorn something is to make it more beautiful.

clue.text: Concerning 2's limits

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "Concerning 2's limits" (scan agrees); 2-down is ROMAN and no reading of its limits or of 'concerning' builds NAVAL, so a cross-reference or word appears misprinted.

clue.text: Fish found by poet on the heather

parts.note: Thomas Gray, author of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A fish turned up by a poet lying among the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Salt goes up about a penny at one time

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about, surrounding, the a and the penny
in a down clue, up means the word goes is read from bottom to top

parts.note: d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: The price of salt rises by about a penny at some point in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GOES into SEOG, and 'about' wraps that round A plus D, the old British penny (from Latin denarius).
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, as is an old sea dog.

clue.text: Service is a foreign one, in general

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "Service is a foreign one, in general" (scan agrees); UN (foreign one) in COMMON gives COMMUNON, and no clue word supplies the extra I of COMMUNION without 'one' doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Service is a foreign one, in general

clue.text: Cleverness on part of author?

indicators.note: only a part of the word Cleverness is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A question of whether a writer's cleverness shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; the run sits inside cleverness. The question mark flags that author is defined by one example, the French writer of Around the World in Eighty Days.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was a French novelist famed for science-fiction adventures.

clue.text: The sort of gun the seconds supply

definitions.meaning: a gun fired at intervals of sixty seconds as a signal of mourning or distress
sixty seconds together make up this unit of time

explanation.definitionFit: A gun fired every sixty seconds at funerals carries this name, and sixty seconds add up to it.

clue.text: Used key politician to get Doyle replaced

parts.note: E is a musical key
MP, Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the letters of the name are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A politician of note had Doyle replaced with someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used has been put to work, i.e. employed.

clue.text: Issue singular form of book ?

definitions.meaning: an edition of a magazine or periodical
The fourth book of the Old Testament; drop its plural s

explanation.definitionFit: A magazine issue is identified by its edition count, and the Old Testament's fourth book loses its plural ending.

clue.text: Someone on shift carries mineral also

indicators.note: the first word carries the second within it

parts.note: a mover is someone who shifts things, such as furniture
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A shift worker also carries some mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone on shift' suggests a worker on a shift rota, but it means one who shifts things such as furniture; 'carries' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover is an adverb adding a further point, like besides or in addition.

clue.text: Making it possible for East to> catch fish

parts.note: to nab is to catch
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Allowing the East to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make something possible, so the participle describes doing that.

clue.text: Vulgar expression, perhaps — could it mean pub-crawling?

definitions.meaning: an uncouth or ungrammatical usage in language
split as bar plus bar plus ism, it could suggest a doctrine of going from bar to bar

explanation.definitionFit: A crude non-standard usage is condemned by purists, and split up the word suggests a habit of visiting one pub after another.

clue.text: Brave enemy showing fear ?

definitions.meaning: a Native American warrior was called a brave, and his enemy was the white settler
a face gone white with fright

explanation.definitionFit: Westerns had Native American warriors call the white settler by this name, and a frightened person has a blanched complexion.

clue.text: Shot disfigures somebody

parts.note: marks means spoils the surface of, disfigures
a man is somebody, a person

explanation.surface: A gunshot wound leaves someone scarred.
explanation.definitionFit: A good shot is a skilled marksman, someone who hits the target.

clue.text: Fashionable doctor to write on food

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
a dish is a prepared serving of food

explanation.surface: A trendy doctor is going to write about cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the doctor sits on top of the food; 'to write' only joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means in the current style, in vogue.

clue.text: Such was Mrs Siddons' muse

parts.note: Sarah Siddons, the great 18th-century actress, was painted by Reynolds as the muse of drama's darker side, Melpomene

explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Siddons was famed for her roles in serious drama, and Reynolds portrayed her as the muse of that genre.

clue.text: " Thy hyacinth hair, thy — - face" (Poe)

parts.note: a line from Edgar Allan Poe's poem To Helen, with the adjective before face missing

explanation.definitionFit: Poe's To Helen praises the beauty of ancient Greece, so the missing word describes a face of timeless Greek beauty.

clue.text: Tubby philosopher

parts.note: tubby suggests stout, but this Greek Cynic thinker was said to live in a large tub or jar

explanation.definitionFit: The Cynic philosopher of Sinope was famed for living in a large earthenware jar in Athens.

clue.text: More paper ?

definitions.meaning: a special edition of a newspaper issued outside its usual schedule

explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is surplus, and a newspaper's special late edition carries the same name.

clue.text: Three articles follow — beginning to bear fruit

indicators.note: the three articles come after the first letter
the beginning of the word bear is its first letter

parts.note: an, an and a are three indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Three items of evidence suggest something is starting to yield results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' sounds like items, but grammatically means a, an or the.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long curved tropical fruit.

clue.text: Agreement has replaced nurses abroad

parts.note: ay, also spelt aye, is a word of agreement

indicators.note: the letters of has are put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An agreement has brought in new nurses from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayah was a native nursemaid or maid in India and other former colonies, so they are nurses abroad.

clue.text: Biblical character put his head under it

indicators.note: in a down entry the head letter goes under the first part

parts.note: to set is to put or place

indicators.note: the head of the word his is its first letter

explanation.surface: A biblical figure ducks his head beneath something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link word pointing back to the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis.

clue.text: Shelter, in a way, from bad weather

indicators.note: the shelter word goes in the way word

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Finding shelter somewhere along the road from the bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleet is a mixture of rain and snow, nasty weather.

clue.text: Paris visitors good and late

parts.note: alludes to the saying, attributed to Thomas Appleton and quoted by Oscar Wilde, that good people from the United States go to Paris when they die

explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that virtuous US citizens go to the French capital after death, so the departed good are its visitors.

clue.text: Brave a hostile reception, as Sir Malcolm used -to do

definitions.meaning: to accept criticism or punishment for one's actions
Sir Malcolm Sargent, the conductor, stood facing the orchestra and its scores

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means confronting the consequences, and a conductor such as Sargent literally stands looking at the orchestra's scores.
